and source this file from your PowerShell profile.

## Use Shipyard from an AI assistant (MCP)

`shipyard mcp serve` runs a Model Context Protocol server, so an
assistant such as Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor or Codex can list, inspect, rebuild and configure your
environments, read service logs, manage volumes, and verify a pushed change against its environment.

`shipyard mcp serve`

Then ask things like:

`web`
`api`

`worker`

See the MCP guide for setting it up in other clients, configuration, the full tool list,
the `verify` prompt, and troubleshooting.

`verify`

## About [...] It never asks anything or waits for input. The check runs in the background while your command runs; if it hasn't
finished when the command does, the CLI waits at most a second for it. That only happens when it's asking GitHub, about
once a day or to fetch release notes you missed. The first run after an upgrade made any other way, such as
`brew upgrade`, shows those notes.

`brew upgrade`

The message goes to stderr, and only when stderr is a terminal. It's never shown in CI, inside AI coding agents that
identify themselves (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor's agent, Gemini CLI), or for `shipyard mcp serve`. To turn it off, set
`SHIPYARD_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` or add `update_check: false` to `~/.shipyard/config.yaml`. [...] ## Repository files navigation

# The Shipyard CLI

A tool to manage Ephemeral Environments on the Shipyard platform.

Using an AI assistant? The CLI includes an MCP server: see Use Shipyard from an AI assistant.

## Installation

Linux and macOS

`curl  | bash`

It installs to `/usr/local/bin`, using `sudo` only if it can't write there. To install somewhere else, such as a
directory you own, set `SHIPYARD_INSTALL_DIR`:

`/usr/local/bin`
`sudo`
`SHIPYARD_INSTALL_DIR`
`curl  | SHIPYARD_INSTALL_DIR="$HOME/.local/bin" bash`

Windows
Navigate to the releases page and download the executable for
Windows.

Homebrew

`brew tap shipyard/tap
brew install shipyard`

results.title: GitHub - shipyard/shipyard-plugins: Shipyard plugin for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Kiro: the Shipyard MCP server plus a usage skill · GitHub
results.content:
- Cursor: set Auto-Run first. With Auto-Run on and MCP Tools Protection off, Cursor runs every Shipyard tool without asking, including ones that stop or rebuild environments. In Cursor Settings, Auto-Run, choose Ask Every Time or turn on MCP Tools Protection. The plugin's server runs in the Cursor app only: `cursor-agent` doesn't load it.
- Use the plugin or a hand-added server, not both. If you added `shipyard mcp serve` to your client yourself, remove it first (for example `claude mcp remove shipyard`). Codex is the exception: a `[mcp_servers.shipyard]` entry replaces the plugin's server. [...] - Read-only tools list environments, builds, services, logs, volumes, snapshots and environment variables (hidden values masked).
- Other tools stop, rebuild, restart, update branches, set or delete environment variables, reset or restore volumes, and create environments. Claude Code and Codex ask before using them unless you allow them. Cursor asks only if Auto-Run is set as above. Kiro's CLI runs tools without asking; see the per-client settings below.
- `exec_service` (run a command in a container) is off unless you enable it.

For unattended agents, allow only the read-only tools. The plugin's tools have different names from a hand-added server's (in Claude Code, `mcp__plugin_shipyard_shipyard__`). Per-client settings are in Permissions and least privilege. [...] `shipyard-hosted` connects your agent to Shipyard's hosted MCP server (` instead of running the CLI. After installing, connect it from your client: `/mcp` in Claude Code, `codex mcp login shipyard` in Codex. Your browser opens Shipyard: sign in, pick the organization the agent works in, and allow access. Your client keeps the token; the plugin holds none.

results.title: How to let Claude Code, Cursor and Codex review your visual diffs
results.content:
Cursor then displays a Needs login prompt; click it to open the Argos consent page. According to Cursor's MCP documentation (checked October 2026), `mcp.json` can only pin OAuth scopes when you configure static client credentials, so pick the read-only scopes on the consent page instead. Cursor asks for approval before it runs an MCP tool by default: leave that on for this server.

## How do you add it to Codex?

The quick way:

```
codex mcp add argos --url  codex  mcp  add  argos --url 
```

When a server supports OAuth, `codex mcp add` starts the sign-in right away and requests every scope the server advertises (source), so uncheck the write scopes on the consent page. For a read-only setup that doesn't depend on that, write the entry yourself and log in afterwards: [...] In interactive sessions, Claude Code asks each teammate to approve a project server from `.mcp.json` before it connects. To block review actions even for someone who granted more scopes, deny the write tools in `.claude/settings.json`. MCP tools are named `mcp____`:

```
{{ "permissions": { "permissions": { "deny": [ "deny": [ "mcp__argos__createReview",  "mcp__argos__createReview", "mcp__argos__dismissReview",  "mcp__argos__dismissReview",  "mcp__argos__ignoreChange"  "mcp__argos__ignoreChange" ] ] } }}}
```

## How do you add it to Cursor?

Add the server to `.cursor/mcp.json` for one project, or to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` for all of them:

```
{{ "mcpServers": { "mcpServers": { "argos": { "argos": { "url": "  "url": " } } } }}}
``` [...] `claude mcp login` opens the Argos consent page in your browser; running `/mcp` inside a session does the same. On that page you choose which organizations to share and which scopes to grant.

To share the setup with your team, commit a `.mcp.json` file at the repository root instead. Claude Code needs `"type": "http"` for a URL entry, and `oauth.scopes` pins the scopes it requests, here read-only:

```
{{ "mcpServers": { "mcpServers": { "argos": { "argos": { "type": "http",  "type": "http", "url": "  "url": " "oauth": { "oauth": { "scopes": "profile projects:read comments:read"  "scopes": "profile projects:read comments:read" } } } } } }}}
```
